cause: Fungus Venturia inaequalis, surviving in fallen leaves.
symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves
Dark, corky, cracked spots on fruit
Early leaf fall
favorable_conditions: Leaves staying wet for many hours
treatment: Spray a registered fungicide such as captan, mancozeb or a triazole (e.g. hexaconazole) at label dose from bud break, repeating as per label during wet weather.
Remove and destroy badly infected leaves and fallen debris; do not compost them.
prevention: Collect and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Prune for open canopy and good air flow
fertilizer_guidance: Follow your Soil Health Card; avoid excess nitrogen, which makes leaves soft and more susceptible.
Adequate potassium improves disease tolerance.
safety_warnings: Use only pesticides registered (CIB&RC) for this crop, at the dose printed on the label.
Wear gloves, a mask and full-sleeve clothing while spraying; do not spray against the wind.
Respect the pre-harvest interval on the label before harvesting.
Confirm the diagnosis with your agriculture officer, KVK or Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551) before spraying.

cause: Bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter, spread by the citrus psyllid insect and by infected planting material.

fertilizer_guidance: Balanced nutrition with zinc and other micronutrients can keep mildly affected trees productive longer, but does not cure the disease.
